posts.title: Extension Rail for Stolle Panda
posts.description: Since, I have short arms and a short length of pull, I need a little help. I built an extension rail for this purpose. The extension rail had to match the 20 minutes built into the rail on the Panda. I had to level it with the dial indicator. Once it was level with the rail, I was able to make the picatinny. After making all the parts, I assembled them on to the action… now I wait for the barrel.

posts.title: First Time in 20 Years.
posts.description: The last time I had a new rifle was 20 years ago. Thought it might be time for a new one. I know folks are waiting for theirs, I have been working on them congruently. I took a lot of the scrapes from prior builds and laminated them together. There are pieces of English Walnut, Koa, Turkish Walnut, Maple and American Walnut. Pistol cap is Curly Koa and Bloodwood. The action is one of the last Stolle Pandas. I weighed my old rifle with the offset scope, it was 15 pounds. The new rifle will hopefully be a little lighter. I’m hiding this rifle from Trudy. She might want to abscond with it, because it looks like a patch work quilt. Sue and Clare think it’s amazing. Next post will be about the rail extentensions. Without further ado, here is the rifle of many colors.

posts.title: Fun with Clamps
posts.description: Yet again, Clare asked our fearless woodworker, “Do you have enough clamps.” His response, “No.” Wonder what this will look like in the end….. Stay tuned.
